title: A Train Crash in England May Have Been Caused by a Bumpy Track
summary: Imagine riding a train and suddenly feeling it bump and shake. Then the train tips over and slides down a hill! That's what happened last Thursday near Lewes, England. A train with eight cars was going from London to Eastbourne. It derailed—that means it came off the tracks. Three cars tumbled down an embankment. Thirty people were hurt. Two were seriously injured, but everyone is out of the hospital now. Investigators are trying to figure out why it happened. They found an "irregularity" in the track—like a bump or a bend. They also got reports from passengers on other trains who said the ride felt rough at that same spot. The train was going about 65 miles per hour, which is under the speed limit of 70. The driver had started to brake. But the weather might have played a part. It was very hot and dry—up to 33°C (91°F). The ground under the tracks is made of clay. Clay can move when it gets dry or wet. That might have made the track shift. The Rail Accident Investigation Branch is now looking at how the track was inspected and maintained, and whether the hot weather made things worse. Network Rail and the train company said they are sorry. They said they will fix any problems to make the railway safer. The government said safety is the top priority. So next time you ride a train, remember that engineers are always checking the tracks to keep you safe.
why_it_matters: A bumpy train ride can be scary, but engineers inspect tracks and use safety rules exactly so everyday trips to school or family stay safe.

background_read: Trains in Britain run on tracks managed by Network Rail (the company that owns and looks after most of Britain's railway tracks).
When a crash happens, the Rail Accident Investigation Branch (a special safety team) examines the track, the train, and the weather.
Hot weather can be dangerous because clay under the tracks can move when it gets dry or wet.
Article_Structure: WHO: Passengers on a London-to-Eastbourne train, plus investigators from the Rail Accident Investigation Branch.
WHAT: An eight-car train derailed near Lewes; three cars tumbled down an embankment and thirty people were hurt.
WHERE: The crash happened near Lewes, England, on the railway line between London and Eastbourne.
WHY: Investigators found an irregularity in the track and are checking whether hot, dry weather shifted the clay under the rails.
